plan: This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, as this doesn't affect the price paid if you win (that's determined by the second-highest bid), but ensures you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, maximizing expected profit. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above risks losses. I'll bid my true value of $15.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay exactly that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. There's no incentive to shade my bid since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding below value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above value risks losing money. With value $42, the optimal bid is $42.
